title: PrioPEG: Primarily implementable group-based physiotherapy and occupational therapy
summary:
For many physiotherapy and occupational therapy measures, both individual and group therapies are equally suitable according to the Remedy Directive. For some indications, group therapy may even be more suitable – both from a therapeutic perspective and for cost reasons. However, practices offer few group therapies, despite the fact that, given the growing shortage of skilled professionals, they could create therapy capacity and reduce waiting times. Digitally supported group therapies could also help address under-provision in rural areas. The reasons for the less frequent implementation of group therapies are partly due to therapeutic, financial, and practical barriers, as well as organizational effort.
The goal of the project is to increase the group therapy rate for two physiotherapy or occupational therapy indications for which both individual and group therapy are suitable. To achieve this, a guideline for implementing group therapy will be developed. Patients and therapists will be surveyed about their experiences, and the requirements for the guideline will be gathered. Additionally, findings from effectiveness research and implementation science will be incorporated. A project advisory board, composed equally of patient, insurance, and therapy representatives, will accompany the development of the guideline. The guideline will then be tested in both analog and digital (tele-group therapy) practice settings to assess its feasibility and acceptance. Furthermore, a tool-box will be created that establishes verifiable criteria to help identify and prioritize further group therapies that can be appropriately and primarily implemented in practice.
The guideline and tool-box will be made available to interested therapy practices and professional associations through an online portal. They can be used nationwide, thus contributing to the continuous increase in the group therapy rate.
conditions: Group-appropriate PT/ET measures, which are prioritized and developed in consensus conferences with patient, therapist, health insurance, and physician representatives. Result of work package 1.
